quote.text: Fiction is that strange, smoky thing that writer don't entirely own, even if they think they do. Where does it come from? Our past, our present, our reading, our imagination - yes. But perhaps from premonitions of our future, too? How else can it be that like the characters in my second novel, "The Ministry of Utmost Happiness", I am too, am now the caretaker of a sort of grave in the gounds of a sort of guesthouse? It's outlandish. It keeps me awake at night. But then I ask myself, Why should we know eveything?

The last two hours of the drive to Dehradun took us through a national park. I have a vivid memory of one of those journeys. It was a clear, beautiful night. We passed a buffalo cart with a lantern tied behind it for a taillight. The driver of the cart was lying on his back, singing to the stars, confident that his buffalo wold take him home. I remember feeling jealouse of him. I remember thinking that no matter how long and hard we fought, in India no woman of any religion, class, caste, or creed would ever feel safe enough to sing to the stars on a lonely highway while her buffalo took her home.
I wanted to think alone. I wanted to know what I thought about when I thought alone. That desire came from nowhere, and it was desparate. Like hunger. Like sleep. Like sex.

Everything I had run away from came running back to me. Ayemenem and all its creatures crowded into my brain. The Cosmopolitans lined up for an identification parade. Mrs. Roy loomed over them all. The friends with whom I had fished and played on the banks of the rive reappeared and challenged me to swim with them. The Meenachil, my slow green river with all her undercurrents, metaphoric as well as literal, appeared and said, "Can you tell me what the fish are thinking? Or explain what the moon is doing floating around at night when she really should be in the sky? Can you describe the sound of boatmen's oars?" And I said, "Yes. Wihtout a doubt, I can. I can see you so celarly, I can feel you so near me, it's as though I never went away."
